prompt:
$P(A)=0.6$, $P(B)=0.5$ and $P(A\mid B)=0.4$.

**(a)** Find $P(A\cap B)$ and $P(B\mid A)$. **[3]**

**(b)** State, with a reason, whether $A$ and $B$ are independent. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $P(A\cap B)=P(A\mid B)P(B)=0.2$ **(A1)**; $P(B\mid A)=\dfrac{0.2}{0.6}=\dfrac13$ **(M1)(A1)**

**(b)** $P(A\mid B)=0.4\ne P(A)=0.6$, so not independent **(R1)**

prompt: Show that if $A$ and $B$ are independent then $P(A\mid B')=P(A)$.
markscheme:
$P(A\cap B')=P(A)-P(A\cap B)=P(A)-P(A)P(B)$ **(M1)** $=P(A)\big(1-P(B)\big)=P(A)P(B')$ **(A1)**

So $P(A\mid B')=\dfrac{P(A)P(B')}{P(B')}=P(A)$ **(AG)(R1)** — whether or not $B$ happens, the probability of $A$ is unchanged.
